name: fraction-shape
title: Fraction of a shape
tagline: Bar, circle or grid split into equal parts and shaded for a fraction; a common-denominator partition derived for adding, equivalence and of-amount.
description: A shape — a bar, a circle or a grid — split into equal parts and shaded to show a fraction of the whole. You choose the shape and write the fractions as n/d; the model derives the partition (the lowest common denominator of the fractions, so 1/3 and 1/4 split the shape into twelfths), shades each fraction's parts in a distinct colour, builds a running sum or difference, renders an improper result across extra whole-shape copies as a mixed number, and — given a `whole` amount — works out each part's value and the shaded total. One fraction draws "shade 3/4 of this shape"; two fractions on the common partition draw "1/3 + 1/4 = 4/12 + 3/12 = 7/12" with the common denominator made visual; a fraction on a finer partition draws equivalence (1/2 = 3/6); a fraction with `subtract` is taken away. Occlude a fraction's label or the result for a question, highlight the answer, or leave the fractions out for a blank partitioned shape to shade. v1 is static (the host can step a staged build); shading is not yet interactive.
whenToUse: Reach for this whenever a fraction is taught as part of a whole shape: shade a fraction of a bar / circle / grid, a fraction of an amount, add or subtract fractions on one shape, show equivalent fractions, or turn an improper fraction into a mixed number. Write the shape and the fractions; every shaded count, the partition, the sum and the mixed form are derived. Common configurations: fraction of a shape — one fraction, e.g. shape "circle", fractions [{ n: 3, d: 4 }] (shade 3/4); leave fractions empty (or omit) with `parts` set for a blank answer space to shade. Add on a common denominator — two or more fractions with different denominators, e.g. [{ n: 1, d: 3 }, { n: 1, d: 4 }]; omit `parts` and the shape is cut into their LCM (12), each addend shaded in its own colour, and the result line shows "1/3 + 1/4 = 4/12 + 3/12 = 7/12". Subtract — set `subtract: true` on the fraction being taken away. Fraction of an amount — add `whole` (and `unit`): "3/4 of 20 = 15", with show.partValues to write each part's worth. Equivalence — one fraction on a deliberately finer partition, e.g. fractions [{ n: 1, d: 2 }] with parts 6 → the half reads as 3/6 ("1/2 = 3/6"). Mixed and improper — an improper fraction such as [{ n: 7, d: 3 }] fills two whole shapes and a third; result.mixed (default on) prints "7/3 = 2 1/3". Questions — occlude a fraction label ("what fraction is shaded?") or result.occlude ("what is the total?"), highlight the answer. Keep the same shape and partition across a lesson so pupils track one picture; change only what is shaded, occluded or highlighted. A staged build reads well: open on the empty partitioned shape, shade one fraction per stage, reveal the sum last. Switch model to compare or order fractions by aligning several whole bars (number/fraction-wall), for a ratio share or an authored-segment "of an amount" bar (number/bar-model), or to read a percentage off a 100-square (number/percentage-square). Synonyms a teacher might use: fraction of a shape, shade the fraction, parts shaded, fraction of an amount, adding fractions, common denominator, equivalent fractions, mixed number, improper fraction, top-heavy fraction, numerator, denominator, halves thirds quarters fifths.

shape.description: The figure split into equal parts. "bar" — a rectangle cut into equal vertical strips (the default; clearest for adding and for amounts). "circle" — a disc cut into equal sectors from 12 o'clock clockwise (the pie/pizza picture). "grid" — a rectangular array of equal cells filled in reading order (good for larger denominators). Default "bar".

parts.description: How many equal parts the whole is divided into — the partition, i.e. the common denominator made visible. OMIT to derive it as the lowest common multiple of every fraction's denominator (1/3 and 1/4 → 12; a single 3/4 → 4). Set it to draw a deliberately COARSER common denominator (1/2 + 1/4 on parts 8) or, with no fractions, a blank shape of this many parts to shade. A value that is not a common multiple of every denominator is ignored in favour of the derived LCM.

items.description: One fraction drawn on the shape: its n parts of d shade a contiguous block in a distinct colour. Several fractions tile the same shape in reading order (left→right on a bar, clockwise on a circle, row by row on a grid) so a sum is built piece by piece. Each fraction is re-expressed over the shared partition automatically (1/3 on twelfths shows as 4 parts).

n.description: Numerator — how many of this fraction's OWN d parts it represents. n may exceed d (an improper fraction such as 7/3): the shaded run then spills into extra whole-shape copies. 0 shades nothing.

d.description: Denominator — how many equal parts this fraction divides the whole into. The shape's actual partition is the LCM of every fraction's d (or the `parts` override), and this fraction shades n × partition ÷ d of those parts.

subtract.description: Take this fraction AWAY instead of adding it: its parts are removed from the end of the shaded run and drawn struck-through (dashed grey), and the result line subtracts it ("3/4 − 1/4"). The first fraction should be an added (minuend) fraction. Default false.

label.description: Override this fraction's block label. By default the label is the DERIVED "n/d" stacked fraction. Pass an "a/b" string for a different stacked fraction, or plain words. Omit to use the derived value.

occlude.description: Render this fraction's label as "?" — the "name this fraction" hook. The parts stay shaded and correct; only the printed value is hidden (and it shows as "?" inside the result line so the total cannot leak it). Default false.

highlight.description: Shade this fraction amber instead of its categorical colour — result/answer emphasis (e.g. the part the question is about). Default false; reserve for emphasis, not as a default fill.

fractions.description: The fractions to draw, combined left to right. One fraction shades a single block; several tile the shape in reading order so a sum (or, with `subtract`, a difference) is built piece by piece, each in its own colour. Omit or leave empty for a blank partitioned shape (an answer space to shade).

whole.description: The amount the WHOLE shape is worth — turns the figure into "a fraction of an amount". Each part is then worth whole ÷ parts, and the result line reads e.g. "3/4 of 20 = 15". Pair with show.partValues to print each part's value inside the cells. Omit for a pure fraction (no amount).

unit.description: Unit for the `whole` amount, shown in the readout — "£", "cm", "kg", "marbles". A "£" prefixes its number ("£15"); other units follow it ("15 cm"). Only meaningful with `whole`. Omit for a bare number.

result.description: The derived readout line beneath the figure — the sum/difference of the fractions, the equivalence, or the "of an amount" value. Include to control it; sensible defaults apply when omitted.

show.description: Show the result line. Default: true when there is something to derive (a sum of two or more fractions, a fraction on a finer partition, or a `whole` amount); false for a single plain fraction whose value is already its block label. Set false to suppress it, true to force it.

occlude.description: Render the final result as "?" — "what is the total?" / "what is 3/4 of 20?". The steps before it (e.g. "4/12 + 3/12 =") stay visible; occluded fractions stay "?" within them. Default false.

mixed.description: Render an improper result (numerator ≥ denominator) as a MIXED number — 7/3 shown as "2 1/3". Default true. Set false to keep the top-heavy form (7/3). No effect on a proper result.

highlight.description: Amber the final result for answer emphasis. Default false.

grid.description: Layout for shape "grid" only — how the `parts` cells are arranged. Omit to derive a near-square arrangement (12 → 4×3, 100 → 10×10). Ignored for bar and circle.

cols.description: Number of columns. With rows omitted, the rows are derived as ⌈parts ÷ cols⌉. A 10 for 100 parts gives the hundred-square look.

rows.description: Number of rows. With cols omitted, the columns are derived as ⌈parts ÷ rows⌉.

fractionLabels.description: Print each fraction's value on its shaded block. Default true when any fraction is drawn. Set false for a bare shaded picture (e.g. when the result line carries all the labelling, or for an answer space where pupils name it).

partLabels.description: Write the unit fraction 1/parts inside EVERY part — the "count the parts" view that names each piece. Default false (clean). Dropped automatically where a part is too narrow for the label.

partValues.description: With `whole` set, write each part's value (whole ÷ parts) inside every part — so pupils see the amount one part is worth. Default false. Ignored without `whole`.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure; the top padding grows to clear it.

caption.description: Optional line centred below the figure, e.g. a short context note. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.

examples.label: Worked example — three quarters of a bar shaded
Blank answer space — a circle in quarters to shade
The hard case — 1/3 + 1/4 on a common twelfth partition
Occluded question — name the fraction shaded on a grid
Fraction of an amount — 3/4 of 20 with each part worth 5
Mixed and improper — seven thirds across whole circles
